hero.title: Connect your systems. Simplify your integrations.
hero.description: The Hub is a synchronization platform that connects systems through a shared data model and reusable connectors.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.business: Install connectors, configure integrations and manage data exchange between your systems.
howItWorks.development: Build reusable connectors and distribute them to organizations that need to integrate their systems.

dataModel.title: A shared data model
dataModel.description: Connect different systems through a common protocol.

permissions.title: Permissions under your control
permissions.description: Define which information each integration can read and modify.

visibility.title: Synchronization visibility
visibility.description: Monitor the status and activity of your integrations.

security.title: Security and control
security.description: The Hub's security model is based on project roles, explicit integration permissions and independent credentials for each connector.

platform.question: What is The Hub?
platform.answer: A platform for synchronizing data between systems through connectors.

business.question: What is a Business project?
business.answer: A workspace where organizations install connectors, configure integrations and manage permissions.

development.question: What is a Development project?
development.answer: A workspace where developers build, configure and distribute connectors.

technical.question: Do I need technical knowledge?
technical.answer: Installing and configuring an existing connector does not require building an integration from scratch. Creating new connectors requires programming knowledge.

guide.quickstartText: Create a Development project, define a connector, request the required permissions and publish it. A Business project must install it and complete its configuration.
guide.prerequisites: Data operations require an authorized, correctly configured, active integration belonging to a Business with an active subscription.
guide.environment: Configure the following variables on your connector server. Replace the example values with those of your installation.
guide.businessText: Project that owns data and integrations.
guide.developmentText: Project that develops and distributes connectors.
guide.connectorText: Reusable integration definition with parameters, requested permissions and credentials.
guide.instanceText: Installation of a connector within a Business project.
guide.batchText: Ordered collection of changes that can be applied atomically.
guide.changeText: Registered model operation or configuration event.
guide.propagationText: Delivery of a change to a destination instance.
guide.authenticationText: Protocol operations require a connector token sent through Authorization: Bearer. Keep the token exclusively on your server. Rotate it through the platform if compromised.
guide.installationsText: List authorized installations of your connector and retrieve each instance's configuration before operating.
guide.idText: id: UUID identifying a record within The Hub.
guide.refIdText: ref_id: local record identifier for a specific instance and model.
guide.globalRefText: global_ref: original local reference of the record in the instance that created it. It may be unavailable.
guide.referencesText: Do not use global_ref as a universally unique identifier. Maintain the association between The Hub's UUID and your system's identifier.
guide.permissionsText: Operations are restricted by permissions requested by the connector and granted by the instance. Origin filters can restrict which other instances generate received changes.
guide.modelDiscoveryText: Retrieve the current version and its columns before building requests. Example fields must be adapted to published models.
guide.transactionsText: Begin a batch for an authorized instance. OPEN batches expire after 10 minutes. Write requests register changes without immediately modifying data.
guide.beginText: Store the id returned by BEGIN in BATCH_ID before registering operations.
guide.listText: Queries return active records from the project associated with the instance. Use next_cursor to continue pagination.
guide.commitText: COMMIT applies all registered changes in order and generates authorized propagations. If an operation fails during application, none are applied.
guide.rollbackText: ROLLBACK discards an OPEN batch without applying its changes. A closed batch cannot be reopened.
guide.batchStatusText: If the COMMIT HTTP response is lost, retrieve the batch before starting another. COMMITTED indicates that changes have already been applied.
guide.pullText: List PENDING propagations, retrieve their details and apply each idempotently in your system. The list id identifies the propagation, not the business record.
guide.confirmText: Send OK only after successfully applying the change. Confirmations within a single request are processed atomically.
guide.confirmCreateText: When creating a record in the destination system, you may send its local ref_id with the OK confirmation.
guide.failedText: Report FAILED when a change cannot be applied. The connector can retrieve those propagations again and confirm them as OK after resolving the issue.
guide.setupText: SETUP generates a consistent snapshot of active records in models authorized for CREATE reception. It expires previous PENDING propagations for those models and generates new CREATE propagations.
guide.setupWarning: SETUP does not remove extra records from the external system or replace its deduplication logic. Do not run it periodically without a reconciliation strategy.
guide.settingText: SETTING events notify changes to configuration, permissions and operational status. Retrieve authorized configuration again when appropriate. Missing notifications do not guarantee that an instance retains its permissions.
guide.idempotencyText: Use a stable client_operation_id when retrying the same operation within the same batch. Persist processed propagation identifiers and local references. If a confirmation response is lost, verify its status before repeating external effects.
guide.limitsText: Batches expire after 10 minutes. Write and confirmation requests support up to 100 items. List endpoints support up to 200 items per page.
guide.errorsText: Check the HTTP status and error code before deciding whether to retry. Do not automatically retry validation, authorization or conflict errors.
guide.typescriptText: The following example registers and commits a creation using native fetch. Adapt its fields to the current model and add operation persistence and error recovery before production use.
guide.statesNotice: Only OPEN accepts new changes. OK and EXPIRED propagations are terminal. FAILED can transition to OK. An OK instance does not imply that all its propagations are confirmed.
